result.summary: The image shows a two-lane roadway with a marked continental crosswalk and a sidewalk separated by a line of trees. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and markings are present, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks pedestrian-oriented signage or signals.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any stop signs, traffic signals, or warning signs to alert drivers to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Potential Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The bridge support pillars and trees to the left may partially obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers until they are in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image near the bridge structure

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install W11-2 pedestrian crossing warning signs to alert motorists of the crossing location.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add user-actuated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the travel lanes.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a commercial corridor with basic infrastructure including sidewalks and marked crosswalks. However, the wide roadway geometry and lack of traffic calming or signalization create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The corner on the left has a wide radius, allowing vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signalization
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the roadway without the aid of a signal, relying entirely on driver yielding behavior in a high-speed design environment.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles at the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade transverse markings to continental or ladder style for better visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide vertical enclosure and naturally encourage slower traffic speeds through psychological friction.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane commercial street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure exists, the crossing is uncontrolled and lacks advanced safety features like pedestrian signals or curb extensions to improve visibility.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A parked vehicle in the immediate foreground obscures the view of the sidewalk and curb for drivers approaching from the left, and vice versa for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks signals or active warning devices on a road that appears to have significant commercial traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the crosswalk, improving sightlines.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a mid-block pedestrian crossing under a large concrete overpass, featuring a zebra-marked crosswalk and stop signs. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the environment suffers from deep shadows and sightline obstructions caused by massive support pillars.

hazards.name: Low Light and Shadows
hazards.description: The overpass creates deep shadows that reduce the visibility of pedestrians within the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars can block the view of pedestrians waiting to cross from the perspective of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the roadside near the crosswalk

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity, pedestrian-focused lighting to eliminate shadows and improve visibility at the crossing.

interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the crossing to shorten the distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position beyond the pillars.
